title_guess: Derivatives and futures through a temple shoe token, then hedging a falling share with a futures sell (options left for the next video)
recurring_cast: shoe icon (the narrator's new shoes, the first underlying asset)
token_coin numbered 75 (the temple shoe token, later labelled DERIVATIVE)
shoe_rack (a real photo of a numbered temple shoe rack, one slot boxed in yellow)
sad_person (the buyer sitting and crying under the banner)
banner_board 'prices to go up from tomorrow' with a shoe
ASSET box fed by bond and stock certificates, dotted arrow to a DERIVATIVE document
timeline line from '10 Feb 584.00' to a blue 'March END 589.95' futures box
graph_axes with a price path and a shaded loss or gain region
running_examples: shoes bought for 5000; token worth 5000; if shoes cost 15000, token worth 15000
temple deal: buyer pays 5500 after 30 days for the token; market price then 6000, both gain; at 5100 the buyer would lose (spoken only)
share held at 584 on 10 Feb; March futures sold at 589.95

best_moments.why: shoe price and token value sit at two ends of a dotted arrow; when the shoe's 5000 is struck and rewritten 15000, the token's value changes to 15000 too: 'a derivative takes its value from something else' as two linked numbers
bond and stock certificates arrow into the ASSET box and replace the shoe, and the token turns into a contract document: the analogy is converted into the general case on the same canvas

the deal as a band: narrator on the left, buyer on the right, token flowing right and a 5500 cash note flowing left under a Futures document marked 'after 30 days': a futures contract as a two-way swap fixed today for a later date
after 30 days the cash sits with the seller, the shoes with the buyer, 6000 Rs written under the shoes, and both get green ticks: who gained is shown, not told

a timeline from today's spot price (584, 10 Feb) to a blue 'March END 589.95' futures box, and below it the price path falls into a red region with a 284 loss bar; callouts link the stock loss and the futures gain into one net profit tag
in the rising case a red cross on the price path at 700 marks where the futures contract is closed, with the subtraction written on a leader line: the exact point of a decision is placed on the path

weak_moments.why: the same deal band stays still for about 57 s while the voice adds contractual obligation, why the buyer signs, price uncertainty (10000 or only 50-60 more) and 'mental peace'; none of it is drawn
a collage of a real research firm's logo, a real company logo and a real person's photo with a red down arrow; BIE will not use real people or brands
a broker app quote strip for a real company's March futures is copied onto the canvas; BIE must redraw such a quote generically
number mismatch: the futures gain is written +289.85 while the voice says 289.95, and the net +5.95 only works with 289.95

the red cross at 700 and 'close the futures contract' fall inside a 22 s stretch with no recognised speech, so why the hedge is closed early is carried by the picture alone; the following 'profit in both cases' depends on that discretionary exit, which should be checked before reuse
hedging's literal meaning (a fence or boundary round a field) is only a small caption under an app promo overlay; no fence is drawn
the title chip is misspelt 'DERIVATES', and it promises options, which are never taught here (only an untouched Options branch)

segments.teaches: opening: the video will explain derivatives, futures and options with the narrator's new shoes; the shoes were bought today for 5000

elements.what: three-part title chip: derivatives | futures | options (first word misspelt)
a black sneaker
'5000 Rs' under the shoe

segments.notes: 3 change events. The personal object (my new shoes) is the hook; the title leaves before the price appears.
segments.idea: we will learn derivatives with one everyday object whose price we know: shoes worth 5000
segments.shown_as: a three-word title chip over a single shoe icon; the title goes and '5000 Rs' is written under the shoe

segments.teaches: at a temple you leave your shoes in a rack and get a numbered token in return

red temple top
standing person with the shoes at his feet
small numbered token coin appearing in the person's hand, dotted line down to '5000 Rs'

segments.notes: 4 change events. The shoes move into the boxed rack slot and a token appears with the person; the 5000 label moves from shoes to token.
segments.idea: giving the shoes to the rack gets you a token that stands for them
segments.shown_as: person beside a temple with shoes at his feet; the shoes go into a yellow-boxed slot of the rack photo and a numbered token appears in his hand, with '5000 Rs' hanging under the token
segments.example: token worth 5000 because the shoes are worth 5000; lose the token and you lose 5000

segments.teaches: the token's value depends on the price of what is in the rack; so the token is a derivative, deriving its value from an underlying asset

elements.what: framed shoe with 'Price' below on a dotted drop
long dotted arrow from the shoe to the token
token with 'Value' below on a dotted drop

elbow leader from the token up to a DERIVATIVE label
short definition under DERIVATIVE: value taken from the price of an underlying asset (last two words highlighted)

segments.notes: 4 change events. Price and Value are labelled under the two ends, so the pair reads as cause and effect.
segments.idea: a derivative is worth whatever the thing behind it is worth: change the shoe's price and the token's value changes with it
segments.shown_as: shoe on the left, token on the right, joined by a dotted arrow; the shoe's 5000 is struck and rewritten 15000 and the token's value follows to 15000; a leader line from the token names it DERIVATIVE with a one-line definition

segments.teaches: the rack item is the underlying asset; real underlying assets are bonds, stocks, gold, commodities and foreign exchange; a derivative is a financial instrument whose price moves when the asset's price moves

elements.what: ASSET above the framed box

segments.notes: 6 change events. The analogy is converted in place: shoe -> bond/stock, token -> contract. The green arrow at Price is the only sign of 'asset prices move', which the voice explains.
segments.idea: the shoe-and-token pair is the same as any asset and the contract written on it
segments.shown_as: an ASSET heading appears over the shoe; bond and stock certificates arrow into the box and replace the shoe; a list of asset kinds writes on; the token turns into a contract document under a 'Financial Instrument' tag; a green up arrow by Price

segments.teaches: derivatives are of many kinds, mainly futures and options

elements.what: clean pair: asset box with bond and stock certificates, dotted arrow to the DERIVATIVE document

segments.notes: 2 change events. The list and definition are wiped to a clean pair, but the two types the voice names are not drawn here; the futures/options branch appears only at 308 s.
segments.idea: derivatives come mainly in two kinds: futures and options
segments.shown_as: the canvas is cleaned to the asset box and the derivative document alone while the voice names the two types; no branches yet

segments.teaches: story problem: a banner says the shoes' price will rise from tomorrow; a man who can only buy after 30 days (salary) does not know the future price and may be priced out

elements.what: the shoe rack photo again with the yellow slot
temple top, standing narrator, token labelled DERIVATIVE over '5000 Rs'
banner board on two poles: 'prices to go up from tomorrow' with a shoe
man sitting hunched and crying under the banner
'After 30 Days' under the sitting man

segments.notes: 4 change events in about 85 s; long dialogue (why not buy today, salary in 30 days, 5500 offer) over a nearly still scene.
segments.idea: a buyer who must wait faces an unknown future price: that is the risk a futures contract removes
segments.shown_as: the temple scene returns with the token now labelled DERIVATIVE; a banner announcing a price rise pops up on the right and a man sits crying beneath it, tagged 'after 30 days'
segments.example: today 5000; maybe 6000-7000 after 30 days; offer of 5500 accepted

segments.teaches: the futures agreement: after 30 days the buyer pays 5500 and gets the token; both are bound and cannot back out; the buyer signs to remove price risk, not for profit

elements.what: contract document labelled Futures with 'After 30 Days, 5500 Rs', lines joining narrator's token to the buyer
light-blue band: narrator, token arrow to the right, buyer; a 5500 cash note arrow back to the left
'After 30 Days' beside the Futures document over the band

segments.notes: 4 change events, then the band is still for about 57 s (215-272) while obligation, risk and 'mental peace' are explained only in speech.
segments.idea: a futures contract fixes today the price and date of a later exchange, and binds both sides
segments.shown_as: a contract document drops between the two people and lines link token and buyer through it; the scene tidies into a blue band with the token flowing right and a 5500 cash note flowing left, under 'Futures, after 30 days'
segments.example: pay 5500 after 30 days for the token

segments.teaches: after 30 days the deal is settled: the buyer pays 5500 and gets the shoes, whose market price is now 6000; both gain; had the price risen only to 5100 the buyer would have lost, but he signed to avoid price swings

buyer holding the shoes, dotted drop to '6000 Rs'
green ticks over both people

segments.notes: 4 change events. The 5100-loss case is only spoken.
segments.idea: on the agreed day the swap happens at the fixed price whatever the market price is
segments.shown_as: cash and token have changed hands across the band; the token goes back to the rack slot and the buyer now holds the shoes with '6000 Rs' under them; a green tick pops over each person
segments.example: paid 5500, market 6000: buyer saves 500, seller gains 500 over his 5000; at 5100 the buyer loses (spoken)

segments.teaches: derivatives split into futures and options; a futures contract is a way to transfer or reduce the risk tied to the underlying asset

segments.notes: 3 change events. The tree is drawn here, 200 s after the voice named the two types. Options is never opened.
segments.idea: futures is the derivative used to shift away price risk
segments.shown_as: the asset-to-derivative pair returns and splits into Futures and Options; Futures is boxed in yellow and a one-line definition writes on under it

segments.teaches: practical case: you hold shares of a listed company at 584 on 10 Feb; bad news has been pushing the price down and may push it further; you do not want to sell, only to reduce the risk

segments.notes: 5 change events. Real company, real person and a real controversy: BIE replaces all of it with a generic company and a generic 'bad news' card.
segments.idea: a holder fears a fall in the price of shares he wants to keep
segments.shown_as: the asset box now belongs to a person and holds a share certificate priced 584 on 10 Feb, with a dotted arrow to the derivative document; a news collage with a red down arrow pops in at top right

segments.teaches: hedge by selling March futures at 589.95: if the share falls to 300 you lose 284 on the share but gain 289.95 by buying the futures back at 300, a net +5.95 instead of -284

elements.what: blue line from the person at '584.00, 10 Feb' to a blue 'March END 589.95' box with the Futures document

segments.notes: 8 change events. Screen '+289.85' vs spoken 289.95 (589.95 - 300); the net 5.95 needs 289.95. Shown but not spoken: the quote strip's day change figures.
segments.idea: a futures sell gains as much as the shares lose, so the holder's value is locked near the futures price
segments.shown_as: a timeline runs from today's 584 to a blue March-end box holding the futures at 589.95; beneath it a price path drops to 300 inside a red region with a 284 loss bar; a callout links '-284' on the holder to '+289' on the futures box and a green PROFIT +5.95 tag pops over the holder

segments.teaches: opposite case: the share rises to 984 (+400); the futures position is closed at 700 for a loss of about 110; net +290

elements.what: red region removed; a neutral band, then a rising path from 584 to 984 in a green region with a green bar '400'
red cross on the path at 700
leader from the cross: close the futures contract = 700 - 589.95 = -110
dotted curved arrow from the futures box down to that line
beside the holder: 984 - 584 = +400
green PROFIT tag: +400 - 110 = 290

segments.notes: 5 change events. The cross at 700 (496 s) falls inside a 22 s stretch (476-498) with no recognised speech, so the reason for closing early is not in the transcript. Doubtful: the 'profit both ways' result depends on closing the hedge early on a judgement about news; a hedge held to March end would give up most of the 400 rise. Spoken 'sold at 598.95' vs screen 589.95.
segments.idea: if the price rises, the futures leg loses; the holder here cuts that loss by closing the futures early
segments.shown_as: the loss region is wiped and a rising path fills a green region to 984 with a 400 bar; a red cross marks 700 on the path and a leader line writes the futures loss there, with a dotted arrow from the futures box; the holder's +400 and a PROFIT tag with +400 - 110 = 290 complete the sum
segments.example: rise to 984: +400; futures closed at 700: 700 - 589.95 = -110; net 290

segments.teaches: recap: futures is the derivative that moves price risk; using it this way is called hedging, literally a fence round your field
